name: Skyscraper method

card.summary: A looksmax.org-circulated routine of stationary biking, resistance bands, sleep and diet changes that its author says adds length to the legs, spine and other body segments, for a taller look.
card.note: Circulated as a forum guide; no published study has tested it, and growth plates normally fuse in the mid-to-late teens.

quick.overview:
The Skyscraper method is a height-increase guide posted on looksmax.org. It lists body segments its author says can gain length (abdomen, femurs, shinbones, fingers, forearms, collarbone, spine) and promises a taller, longer-limbed frame to those who follow it.

The guide ties its approach to growth hormone, which it describes as produced by the pituitary and released mostly in early sleep and after exercise. Replies on the threads are mixed, and no published study has tested the routine.
quick.how: As written, the guide calls for time, a stationary bike with an adjustable seat, resistance bands and consistency, along with giving up nicotine, alcohol, processed foods and poor sleep. Its framing is that exercise, sleep and nutrition support the hormones that drive growth.
quick.risks: The routine itself is low-intensity exercise and lifestyle change. Medical references note that long bones stop lengthening once the growth plates fuse, typically in the mid-to-late teens for boys, so expectations among adults differ sharply between proponents and clinicians.

lead: The Skyscraper method is a named height-increase routine shared on the forum looksmax.org. Its author lists the body parts they say can gain length: abdomen, femurs, shinbones, fingers, forearms, collarbone and spine [1][2]. People discussing it treat it as a way to look taller through a longer frame, rather than through lifts or surgery.

The guide's stated requirements are time, a stationary bike with an adjustable seat, resistance bands and dedication, plus dropping nicotine, alcohol, processed foods and bad sleep [1]. It frames growth as the product of hormones, environment, lifestyle and genetics, and focuses on human growth hormone (HGH) from the pituitary gland, which it says peaks in youth and is released mostly in the first hours of sleep and after exercise [1].

Replies on the threads are mixed. One reader dismissed the post as a wall of text, while the author said they wanted it posted anyway; another reply questioned the nicotine advice by pointing to short-statured and tall smokers alike and attributing height to genetics [2][1]. No clinical study has tested the routine.

chain: Bike and band work plus sleep, diet and lifestyle changes
Supports growth hormone and bone-forming signals, as the guide describes
Claimed added length in legs, spine and other segments
angle.text: The guide presents the routine as a way to gain length across several body segments and look taller. Its stated mechanism is hormonal support through exercise, sleep and cleaner habits.

infobox: Avoid nicotine, alcohol, processed foods; sleep [1]

paras: The guide opens with a list of body segments where length can supposedly be gained and a short equipment list [1]. It then explains hormones, describing HGH as made in the pituitary gland, stimulating growth of muscle, cartilage and bone, and as raising IGF-1 [2]. It is a second version of the same text, reposted under a title noting the absence of success stories [1].

Proponents argue that sleep quality, exercise and avoiding substances such as nicotine and alcohol let the body release more growth-related hormones, and that this can lengthen several segments of the skeleton [1][2]. Some readers disagree on specifics, such as whether nicotine affects height [1].

Medical references describe the epiphyseal (growth) plates as the sites where long bones lengthen. Fusion typically occurs around 15–17 in boys and 14–15 in girls, after which the bone can no longer lengthen at those plates [3]. Clinicians therefore generally distinguish growth during adolescence from changes in adults. No published study has examined the Skyscraper method itself.

lore.intro: The method appears in looksmax.org threads where users debate height-increase routines [1][2].

claims.claim: Bike and band work with better sleep and diet can add length to many body segments
claims.believers: The author lists abdomen, femurs, shinbones, fingers, forearms, collarbone and spine and says hormones such as HGH respond to exercise and sleep [1].
claims.experts: Endocrinology references state that long bones stop lengthening once growth plates fuse in the late teens, and no published study has tested this routine [3].

claims.claim: Nicotine, alcohol and processed foods should be cut to support growth
claims.believers: The guide lists them as things to ditch [1].
claims.experts: No published study has tested these items in relation to this routine; replies on the thread dispute the nicotine point from personal observation [1].
